name: Google Chrome
summary: Block third-party cookies, enable Secure DNS, and limit telemetry sent to Google.

settings.name: Block Third-Party Cookies
settings.impact: Third-party cookies are the primary mechanism advertisers use to track you across different websites. Blocking them prevents cross-site tracking without breaking most website functionality.
settings.source: Privacy International: Chrome Privacy Guide; ChromeThemer.com 2026

settings.name: Safe Browsing
settings.impact: Enhanced Protection warns you about dangerous sites, downloads, and extensions in real time, even for new threats not yet catalogued. Trade-off: it sends more browsing telemetry to Google.
settings.source: Privacy International: 'Adjusting Chrome Settings to Enhance Your Online Privacy'; ChromeThemer.com 2026

settings.name: Browsing Data Sharing
clickPath: Toggle OFF: 'Make searches and browsing better' and 'Help improve Chrome features'
settings.impact: These settings send browsing data to Google's servers for analysis. Disabling stops Chrome from uploading your browsing behavior to Google while keeping core functionality intact.

settings.name: Site Permissions Audit
clickPath: Set Location, Camera, Microphone, Notifications to 'Ask before accessing'
settings.impact: Many sites are granted location, microphone, or camera access and users forget they authorized it. Resetting to 'Ask' ensures no site silently retains sensitive hardware access.

settings.name: Secure DNS
settings.impact: Standard DNS queries are sent unencrypted, letting your ISP see every domain you visit. DNS-over-HTTPS encrypts these lookups and prevents eavesdropping.
settings.source: ChromeThemer.com Chrome Privacy Configuration Tips 2026; Google Chrome Help
